segments.title: Chương 224: 0225【Toàn là người quen cũ】
segments.content:
Chapter 228 Part 225: What a Small World

"Hero Chen, are you reflecting on your mistakes while facing the wall?" Qin Shanshan joked.

In the Hall of Zhuge Liang, Chen Guiliang stood to the side of the statues, staring at the north wall for a long time.

This drew the others over as well, but they found nothing besides drapery and the wall.

"It's nothing," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Inside the wall were hidden eight stone steles from the mid-to-late Qing Dynasty. The inscriptions were the Former and Latter *Memorials on Taking the Field*, written by a Qing Dynasty Zhuangyuan scholar.

These artifacts wouldn't be discovered until the Hall of Zhuge Liang's walls were renovated during the pandemic.

At that time, Chen Guiliang, not wanting to have a falling out with his startup partners, had retained a portion of his shares and withdrawn from the company, returning to Rongcheng to start a new venture. As a result, he was hit hard by the pandemic, his second venture failed, and he simply decided to lie flat in Rongcheng.

After the news broke about the new steles being discovered at the Wuhou Shrine, Chen Guiliang had even made a special trip to admire them.

Forget it. They'll be found naturally during the renovation.

It's not like they're some critically important cultural relics anyway.

The group continued to stroll around, chatting idly.

The two girls bought a parasol and walked huddled together under it.

Chen Guiliang was getting scorched by the sun. He asked for the location of the gift shop and found that they actually sold hats. So he bought several baseball caps and handed them out to everyone.

"What a huge tomb," Yang Shuo exclaimed, standing before the Mausoleum of Liu Bei, Emperor Zhaolie of Han.

Chen Guiliang said, "Liu Bei was an emperor. For a joint tomb with his two empresses, being buried under such a small hill is already very frugal."

The well-behaved Xu Haibo stood before the tomb. Without any incense, he simply put his palms together and bowed his head in respect.

Qin Shanshan asked curiously, "Why are you paying respects to Liu Bei?"

"Just showing some respect," Xu Haibo said. Then, a sudden thought struck him, and he asked Chen Guiliang, "Hero Chen, where do you think Cao Cao's tomb is? Will it ever be discovered?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It's possible."

In truth, Cao Cao's tomb had been robbed last year.

Two months ago, a villager discovered a robber's tunnel and reported it. The authorities had it filled back in.

Next year, Cao Cao's tomb would be robbed again, and the Cultural Relics Bureau would carry out a salvage excavation. During the archaeological dig, the occupant of the tomb would be confirmed to be Cao Cao.

Qin Shanshan wasn't interested in tombs. She and Bian Guanyue walked a short way around it and complained, "I'm tired, hot, and hungry. Let's find a place to eat."

Bian Guanyue said, "There's food in Jinli next door, but it's not that good."

"Let's go to Jinli and find a place to sit first." Qin Shanshan's legs felt like jelly from all the walking.

So, the group wandered over to Jinli Ancient Street and randomly ordered some fried rice, noodles, and drinks.

As for the taste of the food, it could only be described as passable.

For the girls, strolling through Jinli was much more interesting than visiting the Wuhou Shrine. After filling their stomachs and resting for a bit, Bian Guanyue pulled Qin Shanshan along to explore the ancient street.

They bought quite a few miscellaneous trinkets along the way.

As they wandered into the mid-afternoon, Bian Guanyue stood by the roadside, pointed at a sign that read "Lianhua Fudi," and said, "That bar Tan Weiwei mentioned seems to be called Lianhua Fudi."

"They're open this early?"

Chen Guiliang stepped inside, passed through a row of green bamboo, and found a teahouse in the garden. There were about five or six tourists, drinking tea and chatting while enjoying a guzheng performance.

A waiter came over to greet them. "What would you folks like to drink?"

Chen Guiliang asked, "Isn't this a bar?"

The waiter answered with a smile, "The bar is inside. It can get a bit wilder at night, but it's usually very quiet. Besides alcohol, we also sell coffee and Western food. Guests can also just do nothing, lie on the sofa, listen to music, and relax. Our boss says this is a lounge music bar."

Chen Guiliang praised, "Impressive. A teahouse paired with a lounge bar. You've got a fusion of Chinese and Western styles here, a diversified business model."

"There's more."

The waiter said, "At night, we also sell barbecue out here."

Chen Guiliang was completely impressed.

A true business genius.

Chen Guiliang and his friends chose a cool spot, ordered a few cups of tea, and sat down to chat.

The tea-drinking tourists were all conversing in low voices; very few were actually listening intently to the guzheng performance. Once they felt they had rested enough, they got up and left to continue strolling outside.

A few more people trickled in, but there were never many customers.

But the tea was expensive, so they were probably barely making a profit.

When Chen Guiliang went to the restroom, he glanced into the bar inside. Heh, it seemed like there were only one or two customers.

Probably bored out of his mind, the owner, holding a guitar, came from the coffee shop inside to the teahouse. He said to the guzheng player who had just finished a piece, "You take a break. Let me take over."

At that moment, apart from Chen Guiliang's group, there were only two other tourists drinking tea.

The owner asked, "Does anyone want to request a song? It's free."

Xu Haibo said, "How about 'Qiu Fo'? It's been pretty popular recently."

The owner's expression soured a bit. "Sorry, I don't know any internet songs."

Xu Haibo pouted and said no more.

Bian Guanyue and Qin Shanshan were trying to hold back their laughter. Xu Haibo and the owner's tastes seemed to clash a little.

"Then sing something you know," Chen Guiliang said.

The owner had a temper of his own. He didn't feel like singing anymore. "My throat is not feeling well. I'll have my apprentice come instead."

He put down the guitar, walked into the bar, and a young man soon came out.

Oh, war against the grain, the battle's wild refrain, the ace is gonna play its game!

Zhang Jie sat down and said, "'Qiu Fo' only got popular in the last two months, so I haven't learned it yet. How about I sing 'Ding Xiang Hua'? It's also an internet song."

"Whatever," Xu Haibo said, indifferent.

Zhang Jie sat beside a stone vat with water lilies growing in it. Behind him was an old gray brick wall. He picked up his guitar and began to sing "Ding Xiang Hua."

Chen Guiliang listened to the song while sipping his tea, watching Zhang Jie with great interest.

Xie Na's future husband was currently Tan Weiwei's boyfriend's apprentice?

Before "Ding Xiang Hua" was finished, Tan Weiwei returned.

She spotted Bian Guanyue at a glance, walked over, sat down, and said, "Are these all folks from back home?"

"Yeah," Bian Guanyue nodded.

Tan Weiwei said, "Then we must get to know each other. I'm from Yongnian Town."

Xu Haibo looked up abruptly. "Me too. My parents are both teachers in town."

"My mom is too," Tan Weiwei said, then asked, "What are your parents' names?"

Xu Haibo said, "My dad's name is Xu Qiang, and my mom is Zhou Guiying."

Tan Weiwei said, "Your mom was my middle school homeroom teacher..."

Xu Haibo suddenly realized. "You're Teacher Zhang's daughter? The older sister who always won singing competitions in elementary school?"

"Yes," Tan Weiwei nodded.

"Your mom was my elementary school teacher!" Xu Haibo said excitedly.

Chen Guiliang wasn't surprised that these two were making connections.

In another life, Xu Haibo often bragged about this.

Today could be considered a dream come true for Xu Haibo. In his previous life, he was a die-hard fan of Tan Weiwei but sadly never got to meet her in person. He had only managed to get her autographed photo indirectly through a teacher.

Tan Weiwei stood up and said, "Let's go drink tea in the backyard."

The backyard was small, a private space reserved for friends and family.

The bar owner, Jiang Zhiming, who was Tan Weiwei's boyfriend and Zhang Jie's teacher, was also pulled along to drink tea and chat.

As they chatted, their connections grew even closer.

Xu Haibo and Jiang Zhiming were alumni of the same university.

Qin Shanshan and Zhang Jie were alumni of the same university.

Jiang Zhiming smiled at Xu Haibo and said, "I'll practice 'Qiu Fo' later. Next time you come, I'll sing it for you."

Xu Haibo scratched his head.

Bian Guanyue said to Tan Weiwei, "During the finals, we'll vote for you."

"I'll vote for you too. We're all from the same hometown!" Qin Shanshan chimed in.

"Thank you so much, then." Tan Weiwei had no doubt she would make it to the finals.

Chen Guiliang, meanwhile, was playing on his phone. Xie Yang had sent him a multimedia message, which was the designed webpage for the Hainei.com rankings.

At the suggestion of Editor-in-Chief Chi Siyuan, they ultimately decided to use "Celebrity List" and "Public List," abandoning the previously discussed "Big V List" and "Grassroots List."

Chen Guiliang replied via text: "Okay, let's go with this design."

Zhang Jie had been staring at Chen Guiliang for a long time. He suddenly blurted out, "Aren't you that Boss Chen from the newspapers?"

Chen Guiliang smiled.

"It really is you!" Zhang Jie exclaimed in surprise.

Jiang Zhiming and Tan Weiwei were both confused. "Is he very famous?"

Zhang Jie said, "He's in the papers a lot. Boss Chen's net worth is supposedly over a billion!"

The two were stunned.
